🧩 Lesson 1: Words Have Parts

Many long words are built from smaller parts, like building blocks. When you know what each part means, you can figure out a word you've never seen before.

⬅️ Prefix = a word part added to the beginning of a word
🧱 Base word (root) = holds the main meaning
➡️ Suffix = a word part added to the end of a word

⬅️ Lesson 2: Prefixes Change the Meaning

A prefix goes at the beginning of a word and changes what the word means. Happy and unhappy mean opposite things, just because of un-!

👆 Tap each card to flip it and see the meaning and an example word.

➡️ Lesson 3: Suffixes Change the Job

A suffix goes at the end of a word. It adds meaning, and it often changes the part of speech (the job the word does in a sentence).

💡 kind (adjective) ➜ kindness (noun) ➜ kindly (adverb). Same base word, new job!

🗝️ Lesson 4: Unlock Any Word in 4 Steps

  1. 🔍 Cover the prefix and suffix to find the base word.
  2. ⬅️ Unlock the prefix. What does it mean?
  3. ➡️ Unlock the suffix. What does it mean? What job does it give the word?
  4. 🔑 Put it together and check that it makes sense in the sentence.

⚠️ Watch out! Some words only look like they have a prefix. Uncle does not mean “not cle”! Always check that the base word is a real word.

Let's unlock: The new phone case is unbreakable.

1️⃣ Base word: unbreakable
2️⃣ Prefix: un- = not
3️⃣ Suffix: -able = can be (makes an adjective)
4️⃣ Put it together: not able to be broken ✅ It makes sense: the case can't break!
